solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pastor's first recruits reorganized his favourite books?

indicators.note: reorganized says the letters gathered are shuffled into a new order
first asks for only the opening letter of the word Pastor's

explanation.surface: A minister's leading recruits have rearranged the shelves holding his best-loved books.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor's favourite reading is the Bible, the sacred writings of his faith; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Restrain drink mob

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
to mob someone is to press or crowd round them

explanation.surface: An order to hold back a drunken crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain something is to hold it down or keep it in check, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Group of three, heading off for Brazilian port

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A band of three musicians sets off for a harbour city in Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major seaport city on Brazil's Atlantic coast, named by example.

clue.text: Husband in sympathy, full of meaning

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: pity is a feeling of sympathy

explanation.surface: A husband offering sympathy whose words carry real weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithy remarks are concise and meaningful, packing much sense into few words.

clue.text: French article about prayer editor's forgotten

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, 'a'
re means about or concerning
a collect is a short prayer in Christian liturgy
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor has overlooked a French piece about a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prayer' is COLLECT, stressed on the first syllable: a short set prayer said in church services.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not recalled to memory has been forgotten, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Problem bar going partly for Prohibition?

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tricky pub closure is suggested as a route to banning alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade, so it is a kind of prohibition.

clue.text: Is about time to rest?

indicators.note: about tells us the word Is is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is nearly time for a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit down is to take the weight off and relax, a synonym for resting.

clue.text: Forager: namely, one retaliating

parts.note: sc. (scilicet) is the abbreviation meaning namely
an avenger is one who retaliates for a wrong

explanation.surface: A forager is identified as someone getting their revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: SC stands for Latin scilicet, 'namely', used in scholarly texts.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger searches for food or useful items among refuse, as a forager does.

clue.text: Distinctive smell of leather — good

parts.note: to tan is to beat or leather someone, and tan is also to cure hides into leather

explanation.surface: A fine leather item with a characteristic aroma.
explanation.definitionFit: A tang is a sharp, distinctive flavour or odour.

clue.text: Harry, maybe, holding learner's chart instrument

indicators.note: holding says one piece contains the other

parts.note: Harry Potter is the boy wizard, so Harry is an example of a Potter
L is the abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Harry holds a trainee's navigation tool for marking routes on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry, maybe' points to the surname POTTER of the fictional wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotter is a device for marking positions or courses on a chart or graph.

clue.text: Strength seen in Crimean War — battling back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
seen in says the letters are found within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Physical power was on show among soldiers fighting in the Crimea.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'seen' in the definition, but 'seen in' is the hiding indicator, leaving 'Strength' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn is muscular strength, the physical power of the body.

clue.text: Out of practice — starts to read up suitable texts? Yes

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A lapsed reader wonders whether to brush up on appropriate books.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusty skill has deteriorated through lack of use, like metal left to corrode.

clue.text: Appears confused over right replacement component

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places one piece above the other
confused says the letters of Appears are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something looks muddled about a proper substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges APPEARS to SPAREPA, placed 'over' RT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare part is a duplicate component kept to replace a broken one.

clue.text: Commanding officer, navy and monarch in tricky situation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
ER (Elizabeth Regina) denotes the Queen

explanation.surface: A commander, the fleet and the sovereign all in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a corner is an idiom for being in a difficult position with no way out.

clue.text: Island tour extremely popular — I join parent

indicators.note: extremely asks for the end letters of the word tour

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
dad is a parent

explanation.surface: A trip to an island at its most fashionable, where I meet my father.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger Caribbean island of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Man's glad crone discomfited gossip

indicators.note: discomfited, meaning upset and thrown into disorder, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old woman, pleased at a man's embarrassment, spreads rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandalmonger spreads malicious tales, which makes them a gossip.

clue.text: Active person interrupted by posh Baronet — he's not convinced

indicators.note: interrupted by says the second pieces break into the first

parts.note: a doer is an active person who gets things done
U means upper-class or posh

explanation.surface: A busy person is cut short by an upper-class nobleman who remains sceptical.
explanation.walkthrough: U is a British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter is someone unpersuaded, a person who remains sceptical.

clue.text: Examine American country site, vacant

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America

indicators.note: vacant means the word site is emptied of its middle letters

explanation.surface: Inspect an empty plot of land in a US rural area.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or study carefully, i.e. to examine.

clue.text: Teacher in from France — alluring woman

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster arrives from France with a seductive lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a temptress, from the sea nymphs whose songs lured sailors.

clue.text: Flood in resort — note to follow

indicators.note: to follow says the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
te is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A holiday town hit by a deluge, with a warning to come.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden flood of water or a rush of anything.

clue.text: Rule northern area, grassy

parts.note: a law is a rule

explanation.surface: Governing a northern region of pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is a stretch of mown grass in a garden or park.

clue.text: Expect answer: 50 kilograms maybe by sound of it

indicators.note: by sound of it says a word that is heard, not spelt, is used

parts.note: fifty kilograms is an example of a weight

explanation.surface: Anticipate a reply about a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for it, anticipating its arrival.

clue.text: Destroyed garden building after threat regularly ignored

indicators.note: after puts the shed piece behind the other
regularly ignored means every other letter of threat is dropped

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding in a garden

explanation.surface: A garden shed was wrecked after the threat was not heeded.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashed is slang for wrecked or vandalised, i.e. destroyed.

clue.text: Expression of annoyance upset this brick-carrier?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: doh is an exclamation of annoyance

explanation.surface: A builder curses while knocking over his load.
explanation.definitionFit: A hod is the open trough on a pole a labourer uses to carry bricks.

clue.text: Head teachers' union

definitions.meaning: slang for the head or skull
the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses a nut for the head, and the National Union of Teachers is abbreviated the same way.

clue.text: Titian added here surprisingly?

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the painter Titian slipped himself into a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian, the Venetian painter, gives his name to a reddish-auburn hair colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian hair is a bright auburn shade, so a titian woman has red hair.
